thread:
incident-bot: :loud_sound: PAGING: Elevated 5xx and latency in dedicated pool 'orion-pool' (ap-southeast-1). Tenant: orion-fin (VPC). 5xx = 31% over 3m. Playbook: https://redwood/runbooks/dedicated-pool-5xx
meena (oncall): ack. Oncall here. Marking Sev2 because this is a high-priority enterprise tenant. Pulling traces and starting containment.
josh (sre): I'm seeing queue saturation on the pool and frequent 'KVCacheRestoreError' in the logs. Isolate options for VPC tenant that keep egress stable?
rita (eng-runtime): short-term plan: preserve egress IPs by launching warm standby nodes tagged for the customer's VPC, apply per-tenant flow-control (max-inflight & per-second cap), and if needed remap traffic. Also prepare a failover with a quantized model to reduce memory pressure. Commands below.
rita (eng-runtime): mitigation commands:
```
# create warm standby in same VPC
poolctl create --name orion-standby --gpu-type t4 --replicas 2 --vpc-tag orion-vpc --warm=true
# set per-tenant flow-control
ctl flow-set --tenant orion-fin --max-inflight 40 --qps 150
# prepare quantized fallback model
models promote --name orion-gpt-q4 --pool orion-standby --ready
```
meena (oncall): applying flow-control now. Paste: 
```
$ ctl flow-set --tenant orion-fin --max-inflight 40 --qps 150
OK: flow-control applied for tenant orion-fin
```
deploy-bot: standby create job accepted; reporting back when nodes ready.
harry (reliability): GPU memory trend shows gradual increase on several workers; pattern suggests per-tenant cache retention that doesn't evict correctly during sustained fan-out. If flow-control reduces pressure we'll avoid restarts.
josh (sre): after flow-control 5xx dropped from 31% -> 13%. Good. Standby coming up; plan ramp 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with checks at each step.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: orion-fin 5xx: 31% -> 13% -> 2.8% after full ramp to standby; p95 latency +140ms.
emma (acct-mgr): drafting customer note. Proposed initial message:
"Hi Orion team,

We detected elevated errors and latency earlier today affecting your dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1. We applied flow-control and remapped your traffic to a warm standby inside your VPC which restored service. We're conducting an RCA and will share findings and any proposed credits within 48 hours. Happy to schedule an exec call after the RCA. 

0: Emma, Redwood"
meena (oncall): capture timeline for customer and RCA. Please annotate severe vs degraded windows.
josh (sre): timeline so far:
- 02:10 UTC: incident-bot alert (5xx > 25%)
- 02:11: meena acked; triage started
- 02:13: per-tenant flow-control applied
- 02:17: standby pool requested (warm, same VPC)
- 02:26: ramp to standby started; stepped to 25%, 75% over 6 minutes
- 02:34: traffic fully on standby, 5xx ~2.8%
- 02:50: metrics stable
Observation: hard-failure window ~02:10-02:24 (~14m); degraded ~02:10-02:54 (~44m).
rita (eng-runtime): artifact capture: heap snapshots, batcher traces, KV eviction logs uploaded to /artifacts/orion/2026-03-18/ (id art-1970-orion-01). Preliminary hypothesis: a race in cache-restore when batcher evicts entries during high fan-out leading to inconsistent map state and retries that amplify load.
meena (oncall): assigning RCA owner: rita (owner), josh (SRE reviewer), harry (reliability reviewer). RCA due: 48h.
emma (acct-mgr): exec summary draft for leadership:
"Brief: Service degradation for Orion Financial in ap-southeast-1 dedicated pool. Contained to single tenant; flow-control + warm-standby remap restored service. Investigating KV-cache restore race. RCA and credit proposal in 48 hours." Any edits?
harry (reliability): add: "No customer data exposure; VPC egress preserved during mitigation." Good for compliance.
meena (oncall): handoff note: I'll be offline in 30m. Josh will cover watch window 03:00-11:00 UTC. Josh, escalate to eng if 5xx > 2% or p95 > 350ms.
josh (sre): acknowledged. Thresholds set.
incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: flow-control applied; standby created; routing updated; artifacts archived. Ticket: INC-2026-2177-ORION created. PD link: https://redwood/pd/INC-2026-2177
emma (acct-mgr): proposing provisional 12% credit (enterprise tier). Approve?
meena (oncall): approve provisional 12% per SLA guidelines. Include precise timeline and impact window.
eurita (eng-runtime): (typo correction: rita) RCA plan highlights: reproduce in staging with synthetic fan-out, add additional logging around KV restore paths, collect core dumps, patch to add idempotent restore operation for KV inserts, and add a guard to force-evict stale entries under pathological growth. Also propose adding a per-tenant soft limit with backpressure to the continuous batcher.
josh (sre): adding quick-runbook snippets to internal ops doc for future incidents:
```
# apply per-tenant flow control
ctl flow-set --tenant <tenant> --max-inflight <n> --qps <n>
# create warm-standby in same VPC
poolctl create --name <tenant>-standby --vpc-tag <tag> --warm=true --replicas <n>
# incremental traffic ramp
routing update --from <pool> --to <standby> --tenant <tenant> --percent <pct>
```
meena (oncall): status at handoff: mitigated, traffic remapped to warm standby in-customer-VPC, baseline restored. Monitoring watch window 24h. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: final 5xx = 0.2% (baseline). Severity: Sev2. Incident owner: rita. RCA due: 48h. Provisional credit: 12% offered to Orion Financial pending RCA. Cleanup: revert routing if stable for 24h, complete RCA, postmortem.
emma (acct-mgr): customer acknowledged initial note and requested an exec briefing after RCA. I'll coordinate scheduling once RCA draft is ready.
meena (oncall): handing off. Josh you own watch window. I'll join RCA review as needed. Thanks team.
josh (sre): taking watch. Will alert on regression. :headphones:
rita (eng-runtime): starting RCA write-up now; will link draft to this thread when available.
pd-bot: PD: incident 1970000001 acknowledged; escalation roster assigned.
